What is Wilderness First Aid?
Wilderness first aid, or “WFA," is a generic term that commonly refers to any training course that focuses on prevention, assessment, and treatment for an ill or injured person in a remote environment where definitive care by a physician and/or rapid transport is not readily available. This is defined as being an hour or more away from advanced care.  WFA courses are intended for anyone planning a remote adventure, from lay responders to medical professionals.

events.title: Winter Field Day 2027 – Ham Radio for Scouts
events.location: National Voice of America Museum of Broadcasting, West Chester, Ohio
events.desc:
Every January, amateur radio operators across the country head outdoors for Winter Field Day, organized by the Winter Field Day Association. Operators set up portable stations in the cold and make contacts with other stations near and far. They use voice, Morse code, and digital modes on HF, VHF, and UHF radio bands. Many stations run on battery or generator power and put up temporary antennas, just as they would during a real emergency. The goal is to practice getting on the air when snow, ice, and freezing temperatures make it hard, so operators are ready to help when disaster strikes.
